records.title: Building standards: natural gas.
records.description: From June 1, 2025, to June 1, 2031, counties are restricted from changing residential building standards unless certain conditions are met such as aligning with previously approved standards, neccesity to health and safety emergencies etc. This bill specifically prohibits changes that would ban natural gas use in residential units.

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: transportation impacts: vehicl...
records.description: Amends CEQA to set limits on mitigation costs related to vehicle miles traveled

records.title: Regional transit hub districts: downtown housing developments.
records.description: Would set appropriate land use standards for transit-oriented development in regional centers, streamline approval processes for developments meeting labor standards, and create a revolving loan fund to finance these developments.

records.title: Wildfire: vegetation management: fuel reduction activities.
records.description: Would, on or before January 1, 2028, and every 2 years thereafter, require the Dept of Forestry or a local entity with fire prevention authority to conduct an assessment for severe fire hazard of all undeveloped public lands. Assessment must be posted and submited to the department. The bill would require all public lands, on or before January 1, 2028, to have 200-foot firebreaks on all borders with private property.

records.title: Integrated waste management plans: annual report.
records.description: The California Integrated Waste Management Act of 1989 mandates the diversion of 50% of solid waste must be annually reported, specifically identifying locations for new or expanded organic waste recycling facilities. This bill would clarify that facilities include medium and small compostable material handling facilities.

records.title: Affordable Housing and High Road Jobs Act of 2022: use by right: objective standards.
records.description: This bill, the Affordable Housing and High Road Jobs Act of 2022, aims to streamline the approval process for mixed-income housing developments by allowing them to be built "by right," provided they meet specific site, affordability, and objective development standards. The bill clarifies that these objective standards cannot prevent a development from reaching required residential densities or force a reduction in unit size. It now explicitly prohibits these standards from limiting mixed-use development within a housing project. It also makes a technical change to the definition of "use by right" to clarify that it means no aspect of the development is considered a "project" under CEQA.

records.title: Surplus lands: economic opportunities.
records.description: Existing laws require local agencies notify the public about available surplus land before selling or leasing it. However, under this bill, if a local agency adopts a resolution before acquiring the property that outlines the reasons for the acquisition, planned improvements, and future use, and then disposes of the property to a public or private entity consistent with those plans, those standard surplus land disposal requirements will not apply.

records.title: Supportive housing: prospective tenants: barriers to access.
records.description: Establishes the California Direct Access to Supportive Housing (DASH) designation to expedite access to supportive housing units for individuals experiencing or at risk of homelessness.

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: essential local fire station projects: judicial streamlining.
records.description: Exempts certain fire station projects from CEQA if they are not on specific sites and have contracts over $50,000 under a project labor agreement.

records.title: Energy: Strategic Clean Energy and Critical Mineral Development Zones.
records.description: Establishes a framework for designating "Strategic Clean Energy and Critical Mineral Development Zones" within California to support the state's clean energy goals. The state will identify and designate these zones. Counties can request designation for areas within their jurisdiction that meet specific criteria, including having significant deposits or production potential of critical minerals essential for batteries and clean energy technologies, and at least two of the following: substantial existing renewable energy generation (like geothermal), high geothermal potential, proximity to high-voltage transmission lines, or being part of an adopted regional planning effort for energy or mineral development. Once designated, these zones will receive priority consideration from state agencies for projects and investments related to energy infrastructure, economic development, advanced manufacturing, workforce development, and critical mineral supply chains, with GO-Biz coordinating efforts to support site readiness and attract investment.

records.description: allows for the aggregation of multiple meters for logistics and manufacturing...

records.description: requires each "large electrical corporation" to file by August 1, 2027 a Tier...

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: geothermal exploratory projects.
records.description: Clarifies the definition of a "geothermal exploratory project" under CEQA to include equipment and activities needed to connect wells and reservoirs, temporary roads, power lines for drilling and testing, and other necessary infrastructure.

records.title: Infrastructure-constrained energization areas: energization timelines: environmental review.
records.description: Requires the Public Utilities Commission (PUC) to designate "infrastructure-constrained energization areas" . Qualifying projects in these areas are CEQA exempt.

records.title: Adaptive reuse: industrial zones.
records.description: The Office to Housing Conversion Act, beginning July 1, 2026, allows adaptive reuse projects to be approved by-right in all zones through a streamlined review if they meet certain criteria. This bill modifies existing restrictions, stating adaptive reuse is not allowed in buildings primarily used as high-hazard.

records.title: Regional housing need: affordable housing.
records.description: Allows a local gov't to voluntarily partner with another city, county  or federally recognized Native American tribes to count new housing development projects towards their regional housing needs allocation. To qualify for this arrangement, the housing project must be jointly funded by the partnering local gov'ts with at least $60,000 per unit in awarded funds, and it must include affordable housing units designated for very low and lower income households.

records.title: Planning and zoning: housing element: regional housing needs allocation.
records.description: would extend several deadlines in the regional housing need and housing element allocation process, Specifically, it would give cities and counties more time to form subregional entities, give councils of governments more time to determine subregional housing need shares, and move earlier deadlines for developing allocation methodologies and draft plans, except for a specified 2027 cycle exception.

records.title: Multifamily Housing Program: Homekey: adaptive reuse.
records.description: Proposes changes to Homekey, allowing funds awarded from January 1, 2027, onward to be used for "adaptive reuse" projects.

records.title: General plan: annual report: shelter beds.
records.description: Proposes that APRs should also include the number of shelter beds available for the homeless, categorized by specific types.

records.title: Electricity: large energy use facilities.
records.description: Would require electrical corporations to file separate transmission and distribution tariffs and generation tariffs for participating customers, and it would require community choice aggregators and electric service providers to adopt generation tariffs for data centers by January 1, 2028.

records.title: Streamlined housing approvals: objective standards: review and modifications.
records.description: Would limit a local govt's review of a development site to only the area physically disturbed by construction when determining site location criteria. Would change process for approving modifications to already approved developments by requiring local govts approve them if they align with objective zoning, subdivision, and design review standards in effect when the application was submitted, rather than requiring the same assumptions as the initial review.

records.title: General plan: annual report: suite-style student housing quarters.
records.description: Would require that the HE APR include data on suite-style student housing quarters.

records.title: Transit-oriented housing developments: alternative plans.
records.description: For transit-oriented housing developments, it allows a local agency's alternative plan to reduce the total number of units or residential floor area in one specific transit-oriented development zone by more than 50%, provided the city has a population under 150,000, a majority of the station area is part of a historic district designated before January 1, 2000, and the city has more than one transit-oriented development zone.

records.title: Local building permits: nonresidential private permitting review.
records.description: Would streamline nonresidential building permits by introducing options for private plan review and setting stricter timelines for local agencies. If a local agency cannot provide an estimated timeframe for reviewing a completed permit application or if there's an "excessive delay" ( 30 days or more—used to be 50 days) in their review, the applicant can request the local agency to hire a private entity for plan checking.

records.title: Housing development: affordable homes bonus.
records.description:
Would rename "Density Bonus Law" to "Affordable Homes Bonus Program" and expand income categories to encompass lower, very low, and extremely low-income households within moderate-income definitions. 

Modifies how the base density for calculating bonuses is determined, allowing for the use of a site's entire floor area ratio for residential use, and removes previous restrictions on where density bonuses could be applied within a development. 

Mandates counties adopt procedures and timelines for notifying applicants about their eligibility for bonuses and increases the number of incentives or concessions developers can receive for including affordable units. Housing projects that are eligible for bonuses will be considered "use by right" and subject to ministerial review

records.title: Data centers: water use disclosures.
records.description: Would prohibit local jurisdictions from approving a data center entitlement that would result in the increase of maximum peak water use. Prohibits data centers from being built in critically over drafted groundwater basins and would require applicants provide a water scarcity plan, a water use assessment , and a water supply assessment to the local jurisdiction.

records.title: Housing development: density bonus: student housing developments.
records.description: Existing Density Bonus Law mandates a county provide developers with a density bonus if they allocate 20% of a housing development's units for lower income students. Bill proposes an additional density bonus for developments that meet this criteria, offer 24% of units to lower income students and ensure no more than 50% of units are restricted to lower or moderate-income students.

records.title: Fire safety: fire hazard severity zones.
records.description: State Fire Marshall is required to review fire hazard severity zones every 5 years, independently of the county and publish relevant local ordinances online within 60 days. Bill permits local agencies to apply a higher fire hazard severity across entire parcel if it contains multiple zone designations.

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: transportation impact mitigation.
records.description: Amends CEQA to provide a new option for developers to mitigate significant transportation impacts, specifically those related to vehicle miles traveled (VMT). This bill allows the government body overseeing the environmental review to consider a contribution to the Transit-Oriented Development Implementation Fund as full and complete mitigation for a project's VMT impact. This fund supports affordable housing or related infrastructure projects that are designed to reduce VMT, such as those located near public transit or in areas with good walkability.

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: natural hazards and adverse environmental conditions.
records.description: Amends CEQA to expand the definition of "environment" to include the health and safety of people affected by physical conditions, and it clarifies that a "significant effect on the environment" can include exposing people to natural hazards or adverse environmental conditions. Further mandates that EIRs must include a statement on any significant impacts that might arise from locating a project near existing or foreseeable natural hazards or adverse environmental conditions, or from attracting people to such locations.

records.title: Transit-oriented development.
records.description: Proposes that transit-oriented developpments (TOD) provisions not apply until July 1, 2027. Would broaden the definition of a "historic resource" and removes a previous limitation that restricted the exclusion of historic resource sites to 10% of a TOD zone's area.

records.title: Planning and zoning: housing development: streamlined approval and subdivisions.
records.description:
Would allow applications for housing projects and parcel maps for urban lot splits to be processed concurrently. 

Would permit local agencies to condition the issuance of building permits, grading permits, or certificates of occupancy on the prior approval and recording of a parcel map for eligible parcels. 

Would allow for the conversion of primary dwellings in urban lot splits into condominiums upon request, or for existing units within a housing development to be converted to condominiums, provided they meet state and local laws.

records.title: Water resources: data centers.
records.description: Would require data centers disclose water-use info when applying for or renewing local business licenses, and it would direct state agencies to create guidelines and local planning guidance for improving water efficiency and evaluating data center impacts

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: exemption: wireless telecommunications facility: broadband internet access projects.
records.description: Would make wireless telecommunications facilities and broadband internet projects not classified as small wireless facilities CEQA exempt.

records.title: Housing Crisis Act of 2019.
records.description:
This bill, the Housing Crisis Act of 2019, expands existing protections that prevent local govts from enacting policies that hinder housing development. 

Clarifies that a "moratorium on housing development" includes situations where voters use their referendum power to extend an existing development freeze. Also requires that any initiative imposing such a moratorium must be approved by HCD.

Definition of "reducing the intensity of land use" is broadened to any action that decreases a site's capacity for residential development, including changes to height, density, floor area ratio, lot size, setbacks, frontage, or lot coverage.

records.title: Accessory dwelling units: separate sale or conveyance: condominiums.
records.description: Normally, ADUs cannot be sold separately from the primary residence unless a local ordinance permits their separate sale as condominiums, which includes a safety inspection before the condominium plan is recorded. The new bill proposes to eliminate this safety inspection before recording the condominium plan. It further allows a condominium be submitted alongside a parcel map or tentative and final map, enabling the portion of the property with the ADU to be sold separately from the main residence after recording the plan.

records.title: Residential Care Facilities for the Elderly on Faith-Based Lands Act of 2026.
records.description: The proposed Residential Care Facilities for the Elderly on Faith-Based Lands Act of 2026 would permit RCFs on religious property at certain densities, allowing them to benefit from density bonuses and reduced development and parking standards.

records.title: Housing element: inventory of land: substantial compliance.
records.description:
Would allow for the use of zoning classifications such as an affordable housing overlay, to allow multifamily residential use with specific minimum density and development standards when rezoning for RHNA. 

Also addresses when court finds a HE to be out of compliance despite HCD finding it compliant, stating that the HE will remain in substantial compliance until either HCD finds a new element to be compliant or 275 days after a court order requiring compliance, whichever comes first.
